jobs.title: DIRECTOR OF INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
jobs.description:
**DEPARTMENT:** Information Services




**POSITION:** Director of Information Technology




**SUPERVISOR:** Vice President of Human Resources and Information Technology/Director of Information Services


The Director is responsible for general oversight under the guidance of senior leadership. The Director is responsible for the design, implementation, and maintenance of the healthcare center's core infrastructure equipment and systems. The role involves ensuring the stability, integrity, and security of in\-house voice, data, video, wired and wireless network infrastructure. This role may require availability after hours as needed for network/system maintenance, emergencies, or to respond to cybersecurity incidents.

* Manage and coordinate all IT\-related matters including systems integration, data, wireless communications, mobile technology, telephony, security, and computer hardware and software.
* Oversee the administration and maintenance of computer stations and software for company and clinical operations, ensuring all systems are compliant with health industry regulations such as HIPAA and HITECH.
* Develop and implement network maintenance and growth plans. Oversee the administration of the company's all networks.
* Develop and enforce policy and procedures to ensure the protection of the IT assets and the integrity, security and privacy of information entrusted to or maintained by the organization.
* Manage IT staff, under the guidance of senior management which includes hiring, training, guidance, and discipline. Ensure high team morale through effective communication and timely issue resolution.
* Conduct routine system audits to ensure compliance with the organization's established standards, policies, and configuration guidelines.
* Maintain knowledge of evolving trends in IT infrastructure and cybersecurity and apply new technologies where applicable.
* Create and manage a disaster recovery plan and respond to all cybersecurity breaches.
* Develop a technical process improvement framework to optimize systems, networks, and infrastructure for better efficiency and performance.
* Oversee the development and enhancement of systems, networks, and integrating new systems with those existing.
* Ensure that networks, systems, and data availability meet business continuity requirements.
* Monitor and analyze system logs to identify potential issues with computer systems, networks, and applications.
* Spearhead troubleshooting, systems backups, archiving, incident response, and disaster recovery, providing expert support when necessary.
* Collaborate with senior management as it pertains to relationship management of vendors and support staff that provide hardware, software, system, network, cybersecurity, and solutions.
* Oversee large scale IT projects such as upgrades and deployments, where necessary. Represent the IT department in coordination with project leaders from other departments and divisions.
* Evaluate potential cybersecurity breaches, coordinate incident response, and implement corrective actions.
* Ensure clear communication with all parties.
* Assist senior management with budgetary planning for the IT department.
* Perform any other duties as assigned.




This role requires the ability to prioritize tasks effectively in a fast\-paced environment, strong customer service skills, and a willingness to explore and adopt new technologies that enhance institutional efficiency. The incumbent must demonstrate strong technical skills in network and systems engineering, along with an in\-depth understanding of cybersecurity principles and best practices.




The role should be carried out according to the highest ethical and moral standards, in adherence to the facility’s corporate compliance plan and all applicable laws. The incumbent must adhere to the facility’s confidentiality statement in accessing and safeguarding protected health information (PHI/ePHI) of residents and employees, as necessary to perform job duties.




Dynamic, hands\-on Director of Information Technology to provide technical expertise and leadership in the areas of network, systems, and cybersecurity, as well as project management. The successful candidate will be responsible for overseeing and managing all aspects of our information technology systems and ensuring the seamless operation of our IT infrastructure.




* Bachelor’s degree in information technology, Computer Science, Cybersecurity, or a related field; a master’s degree or relevant certifications (such as CISSP, CISM, PMP) are desirable.
* Minimum of 7 years of experience in IT management, with a focus on network, systems, and cybersecurity; experience in a healthcare environment is preferred.
* Excellent project management skills, with a proven track record of successful IT project implementation.
* Demonstrated ability to lead and manage IT personnel.
* Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to liaise effectively with all levels of the organization.
* Proactive and solution\-oriented, with the ability to anticipate and address potential IT issues before they arise.

jobs.title: Chief Information Officer, Optum Serve
jobs.description:
For those who want to invent the future of health care, here's your opportunity. We're going beyond basic care to health programs integrated across the entire continuum of care. Join us to start **Caring. Connecting. Growing together.**

  

As the Chief Information Officer (CIO) for Optum Serve, you will serve as a strategic technology executive leading the technology roadmap, engineering, IT operations, and platform capabilities that support our federal government clients. Optum Serve is dedicated to helping federal agencies \- including the Department of War (DoW), Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), and Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) \- deliver world\-class healthcare, administrative services, and advanced technology programs.

  

In this role, you will lead a high\-performing technology organization, navigating complex federal regulatory landscapes, contractual constraints, and stringent security frameworks. You will drive innovation, AI products, leverage cloud solutions, and advanced emerging tools, and ensure operational excellence across mission\-critical healthcare systems that serve millions of military members, veterans, and citizens.

  

You'll enjoy the flexibility to work remotely \* from anywhere within the U.S. as you take on some tough challenges.


For all hires in the Minneapolis or Washington, D.C. area, you will be required to work in the office a minimum of four days per week.

 **Primary Responsibilities:**

* Manage and orchestrate the entire IT ecosystem that supports the Optum Serve business including driving overarching technology strategy, AI product delivery, and delivery execution for the Optum Serve business, ensuring alignment with federal healthcare goals and enterprise objectives
* Serve as a senior customer facing technology executive advisor, engaging senior federal customers and internal executives on complex, high impact technology challenges
* Provide thought leadership on federal healthcare technology trends, emerging capabilities, and regulatory considerations
* Lead transformation of the Optum Serve technology operating model, continuously improving governance, value delivery, capability ownership, accountability structures, and organizational effectiveness
* Partner with Growth and Strategy leaders to identify emerging market opportunities, shape future capabilities, and ensure technology investment strategies support long\-term growth objectives
* Serve as a strategic advisor on how technology, data, AI, and digital capabilities can create competitive differentiation in federal healthcare markets
* Partner with business executives to establish transparent prioritization frameworks that align technology capacity with Optum Serve's highest\-value strategic, operational, contractual, and customer commitments
* Establish and mature technology capability management processes, including build, buy, partner, and reuse strategies that maximize enterprise assets while accelerating delivery
* Provide enterprise wide technical and strategic advisory leadership influencing growth, modernization, and digital transformation initiatives
* Shape and validate customer aligned technology strategies and solution approaches for capture, proposal, and pre\-sales efforts
* Identify growth opportunities through market intelligence, customer engagement, and strategic advisory insight
* Translate ambiguous and novel customer requirements into scalable, compliant solution architectures leveraging existing enterprise platforms
* Lead executive briefings, industry day engagements, and solution demonstrations as the senior technical authority
* Advise on integration, interoperability, data architecture, and security approaches across platforms and partners
* Navigate and manage strict federal regulatory requirements, contractual obligations and security frameworks (including FISMA, FedRAMP, FAR/DFARS compliance, HIPAA, and NIST guidelines)
* Lead the integration of advanced emerging technologies and enterprise AI tools, setting strategic technology goals, and aligning talent development with key digital competencies to accelerate modernization
* Champion the ethical and compliant use of technology and advanced analytics, embedding transparency, fairness, and strict data governance across the solution development lifecycle
* Strategically leverage AI, data, and cloud capabilities to solve complex operational problems, unlock new program efficiencies, and deliver robust mission value to federal agencies
* Manage enterprise risk and security postures in coordination with the Chief Information Security Officer, ensuring consistent renewal of federal Authorities to Operate (ATOs) and the protection of sensitive data (CUI)
* Oversee multi\-million\-dollar technology budgets, direct contract negotiations, and optimize vendor partnerships to achieve strong SLAs and financial stewardship
* Build, mentor, and inspire a world\-class technology organization, promoting a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, and customer\-centric delivery

  

You'll be rewarded and recognized for your performance in an environment that will challenge you and give you clear direction on what it takes to succeed in your role as well as provide development for other roles you may be interested in.

 **Required Qualifications:**

* 15\+ years of progressive technology leadership experience, including 5\+ years of executive\-level IT management
* 8\+ years of experience leading technology delivery, IT operations, or systems engineering specifically within federal government contracting environments (e.g., DoW, VA, HHS)
* 8\+ years experience advising executive stakeholders and customers on technology strategy, architecture, and modernization
* 5\+ years of experience managing compliance and contract governance constraints, including FAR/DFARS, FISMA, FedRAMP, NIST standards, and HIPAA
* 5\+ years of direct financial responsibility overseeing large\-scale technology portfolio

jobs.title: Director of IT Delivery
jobs.description:
Description
**About the Role**


The Director of IT Delivery is the primary business\-facing leadership role within IT — responsible for translating the priorities of Agronomy, Grain, and Back Office Operations into a funded, sequenced, and realistic IT delivery portfolio. This role owns what gets prioritized, while Director of Technology owns how well the organization can deliver it — the two roles are intentionally separated so neither business urgency nor technical capacity gets steamrolled by the other.

  

  

**What will you do?**


* Own the IT delivery portfolio and roadmap across all business units, ensuring priorities reflect actual business need rather than whoever escalated loudest.


* Serve as the primary point of business engagement for IT — the person each business unit goes to when they need something funded, sequenced, or clarified.


* Translate level of effort into business terms and vice versa — able to look at a piece of IT work and communicate realistic timeline, cost, and tradeoffs to a non\-technical business stakeholder, and translate a business ask back into scoped, sequenced technical work.


* Own delivery tracking and portfolio visibility in Wrike — maintaining the roadmap, project status, and resourcing views that both business stakeholders and IT leadership rely on for decision\-making.


* Act as Scrum Master for IT delivery initiatives — running sprint ceremonies (planning, stand\-ups, retros) where applicable, removing blockers, and keeping delivery teams and Delivery Leads working against a shared, visible cadence rather than ad hoc requests.


* Own change management and UAT coordination for delivery initiatives — ensuring changes hitting production are reviewed, tested, and signed off with clear acceptance criteria before go\-live.


* Manage risk across the delivery portfolio — identifying, tracking, and mitigating risk on in\-flight initiatives, and escalating proactively rather than letting risk surface at delivery.


* Own budget and resourcing for the delivery function — including any third\-party vendors or consultants engaged to support delivery work.


* Lead and coach the Delivery Leads (Agronomy, Grain, Back Office Ops), holding them accountable for business outcomes, not just completed tickets — even though they don't own technical staff directly. Build delivery\-team skill and capacity over time, not just manage day\-to\-day output.


* Partner directly with Director of Technology on a standing, recurring basis to weigh capacity and feasibility before committing work to the roadmap — prioritization decisions are made with technical reality in view, not in isolation.


* Coordinate with Lead Automation Engineer on location\-level and automation\-related priorities specifically, given that role's dual scope as both a working manager and a prioritization partner.


* Work with Manager, Business Systems \& AI / Business Systems Analyst to ensure delivery priorities reflect what AGRIS and other core systems can actually support — preventing commitments that outpace system capability.


* Escalate and resolve prioritization conflicts between business units competing for the same shared technical resources.


* Report portfolio health and delivery risk to the VP of IT as part of overall IT governance.


Publish an organization\-wide monthly update summarizing what IT is working on and has accomplished — giving business stakeholders outside IT regular, digestible visibility into delivery progress without requiring them to track the roadmap directly.


Requirements
**Requirements of Role:**


* Bachelor's degree in Business, Information Systems, or a related field; Master's or MBA a plus.


* 5\+ years of experience leading IT delivery, PMO, or business\-relationship\-management functions, ideally in a mid\-size organization (ag, co\-op, manufacturing, or similarly operationally complex industries are a strong fit).


* Working proficiency with Wrike or a comparable project/portfolio management tool, with real experience using it to drive prioritization conversations, not just log status.


* Scrum Master experience or certification (CSM or equivalent) required; PMP or ITIL certification preferred.


* Demonstrated ability to translate technical level\-of\-effort into business\-understandable terms, and business urgency into realistically scoped technical asks — this is arguably the single most important skill for the role.


* Experience managing vendor and third\-party relationships in a delivery context.


* Comfortable operating as a translator between business stakeholders and technical teams without owning the technical work itself.


* ERP\-driven environment experience is a strong plus — familiarity with how a core system like AGRIS shapes what's actually deliverable.


* Track record of holding indirect reports (people who don't report to you on paper) accountable through influence rather than authority.

  

  

**Core Value expectations:**


* Thrive Together


* Integrity in Action


* Grow Forward

  

  

**Physical Demands:** The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.  



  

While performing the duties of this Job, the employee is regularly required to talk or listen. The employee is frequently required to stand; use hands to finger, handle, or feel and reach with hands and arms when using equipment. The employee is occasionally required to walk; sit; climb or balance; stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl and taste or smell. The employee must frequently lift and/or move up to 50 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, peripheral vision, and depth perception.

* Create an IT strategy that aligns with Goodwill's strategic direction, which also controls cost, provides scalability and capitalizes on evolving technologies.

* Select, negotiate with, and manage vendors to build effective, results\-oriented partnerships between the vendors and the organization. Establish and implement a process for regularly assessing vendor performance and for holding vendors accountable.
* Work closely with the CFO to identify critical priorities and maintain tight control over spending while meeting the organization’s business needs.
* Lead the development of IT budget, including capital expenses pertaining to technology projects. Develop forecasts for funds needed for staffing, equipment, materials, and supplies. Monitor and approve expenditures.
* Develop and administer IT security strategy, and policies and procedures for network availability, security, and related issues. Ensure overall compliance with mandated standards including HIPAA, PCI, HITECH, and others.
* Manage all IT staff, contractors, and vendors.
* Assume full management responsibility for IT functions and services.
* Plan and supervise the development and delivery of IT\-related training programs for management and technical staff.
* Prepare cost\-benefit analyses for changes in I.T. workflow and systems, find solutions to friction within the organization and enable technology solutions to help reduce costs and improve mission or revenue.

* Develop and maintain an I.T. team and vendor structure that can consistently respond timely and effectively to our internal customers.

jobs.title: Director, IT
jobs.description:
DNSFilter's mission is to protect our customers and partners with products they love to use! We are revolutionizing network security by providing fast, accurate, and reliable threat protection and content filtering. We're a rapidly growing company dedicated to creating a safer internet for businesses and organizations worldwide. Leveraging AI\-driven threat intelligence, DNSFilter empowers our customers to proactively block threats before they impact their networks. We foster a collaborative, innovative, and results\-oriented culture where every team member contributes to our mission of making the internet safer.



We are a security company, and how we run our own systems should reflect that. Our internal IT function has kept pace with a growing company through automation rather than headcount, and it is ready for someone to own it end to end. That's where you come in!


**We are looking for a Director of IT, based in our Tampa office, to own internal identity, endpoints, and employee technology at DNSFilter. This is a hands\-on leadership role, not an oversight role. You will run Okta, Google Workspace, and our MDM platforms yourself while leading one Senior IT Support Analyst, and you will be accountable for whether our controls actually work, not just whether they are configured. The ideal candidate has built an IT function at this stage before, is comfortable in the consoles, and would rather automate a recurring problem than staff it.**


**This role reports to the SVP of Operations and partners closely with Security, People, Finance, and every department that depends on getting access to their tools on day one.**  

  

**This is a full\-time hybrid\-office role for our Tampa (Westchase), Florida office.**

  

**Eligible candidates have worked successfully in a small\- to mid\-sized, fast\-paced, hyper\-growth SaaS start\-up or scale\-up.**



We recognize that people come with a wealth of experience and talent beyond just the technical requirements of a job. If you feel like this job is for you, please apply. We believe diversity of experience and skills, including transferable skills, combined with passion, is a key to innovation and excellence; therefore, we encourage people from all backgrounds to apply to our positions!


**In this role, you will:**


**Identity and Access**


* Own Okta day to day: user administration, SSO configuration, app assignments, MFA policy implementation, lifecycle rules, and Okta Desktop MFA across the fleet
* Own Google Workspace administration, including groups, distribution lists, delegated access, and directory hygiene
* Own the onboarding, offboarding, and change management lifecycle end to end, and be accountable for the number that says access was actually revoked on time
* Partner with Security to define, and own the operation of, the access model for contractors and BYOD users, including what they can reach, how it is isolated from personal use, and how access and company data end when an engagement does
* Reduce the volume of manual access requests through automation, group\-based entitlements, and self\-service, rather than by working the queue faster


**Endpoint and Fleet**


* Own Mosyle for Apple and JumpCloud for everything else: enrollment, configuration profiles, app deployment, patch posture, and device inventory
* Ensure every company device is enrolled through a supervised path, and close the gaps where it is not
* Maintain accurate fleet coverage reporting, including whether our own machines run DNSFilter's Roaming Client under an enforcing policy
* Support the Security team's rollout of endpoint security tooling on the devices you manage


**Asset Lifecycle**


* Own hardware end to end: procurement through Insight and CDW, zero\-touch enrollment and provisioning, asset tagging, drop\-ship to employees, and return logistics
* Redeploy returned devices under three years old before ordering new, and route anything three years or older to certified recycling
* Maintain an accurate record of every deployed device that reconciles to headcount, MDM, and Finance's asset register
* Manage warranty, repair, and replacement, and own the refresh cycle and the budget behind it
* Own retirement: secure wipe, certified disposal, and the documentation that proves a device was sanitized before it left our hands
* Own device recovery from departing employees and contractors, including the follow\-up on equipment that has not been returned


**Application Portfolio and Spend**


* Own the full inventory of business applications, including what sits outside SSO and how it got there
* Manage licenses against actual usage, reclaim what is unused, and bring renewals forward with a recommendation rather than an invoice
* Own the IT budget: build it, forecast it, and be able to explain why spend moved
* Own IT vendor relationships and contracts, and make the call when a tool is no longer earning its cost


**Workplace Technology**


* Own the technology in our Tampa office: the Ubiquiti stack end to end, including UniFi network and wifi, Access with facial recognition entry, and Protect cameras
* Own physical access and surveillance systems in partnership with People Ops and Security, including who has access to what, retention of footage, and handling of biometric data
* Own conference room AV, printers, and shared office equipment
* Make in\-office and hybrid meetings work reliably, because the ones that do not are the ones everyone remembers


**Service Delivery**


* Own the Zendesk helpdesk: intake, taxonomy, priority definitions, SLAs, and customer satisfaction measurement
* Report a small set of IT metrics monthly, and be the person who explains the number when it moves the wrong way
* Publish a service catalog so the company knows what IT does, how to ask for it, and what to expect


**Availability and Continuity**


* Define and run the escalation path for IT incidents, including lockouts, outages, and issues that hit people while travelin

**GATEWAY SERVICE GROUP**

**Director of Technology Systems**  

Shared Services \| Hybrid — St. Louis or Washington, D.C., up to 50% travel  

Reports to: VP, Strategy and Corporate Development  

**$160,000–$180,000 base \+ 20% target bonus \+ equity participation**  

Gateway Service Group is one of the fastest\-growing commercial property services platforms in the country. We have already chosen the systems that will run this company. What we need now is the person who makes them work together — and who holds the vendors delivering them to the standard we set.  

This is not a strategy role looking for someone to pick a stack. It is an ownership role for someone who wants to build one.  

**About Gateway Service Group**  

Gateway Service Group is a growing, private equity\-backed commercial property services platform operating across lot sweeping, day porter, power washing, construction sweeping, and other exterior property service lines, with branches serving St. Louis, Atlanta, Washington, D.C., Dayton, Philadelphia, and Kansas City.  

**Position Overview**  

The Director of Technology Systems owns how our technology platform performs: making the systems we have chosen work together, holding the vendors who deliver them accountable, and turning what comes out of them into visibility the business actually runs on.  

You are not joining a blank page. Our platform decisions are made and several systems are already live; your job is to finish the build, connect it, and get our systems adopted and talking to each other across every branch and every business we acquire.  

It is also a role that reaches across the whole company. Operations, finance, sales, and HR all depend on these systems, and none of them report to you. Credibility does the work that authority cannot — you earn it by making things work, and you keep it by being straight about what is not working yet.  

You will work closely with our sponsor’s technical operating partner, who continues to lead long\-range architecture and cybersecurity, so you are not carrying the strategy alone. And there is room to grow here: we are hiring at Director level for someone who will own more over time as the platform scales.

* **Drive the selected stack into every branch —** complete our ERP, billing, and field service rollouts across all locations, and carry the HRIS implementation — already well in flight by the time you arrive — through go\-live and adoption
* **Deliver the reporting layer —** the three to five executive KPIs the business runs on, plus recurring versus non\-recurring revenue and gross margin by service line by location, built off the operating platforms where the data already lives
* **Own vendor and MSP relationships —** contract oversight, SLA accountability, and licensing across the technology portfolio — including handling first\-level triage internally before escalating outward, and holding implementation partners to the dates they committed to
* **Execute IT controls and access governance —** including segregation\-of\-duties remediation, working through our managed service provider and alongside finance
* **Support systems work on acquisitions —** our integrations team runs each deal; your job is to make sure no integration milestone waits on systems, vendor scheduling, or data capacity
* **Support compliance\-driven technology needs —** including fleet telematics and DOT reporting, contractor prequalification portals, and payroll and HRIS data integrity
* **Put AI to practical use —** identify and implement AI\-powered tools that automate real workflows, along with the governance and usage standards to deploy them responsibly
* **Manage the technology budget —** report rollout progress and vendor performance to executive leadership regularly, and build institutional capability so that no system depends on one person’s knowledge — including your own

**Who You Are*** **Player\-coach:** you design the plan and execute it personally — equally comfortable presenting a roadmap in the boardroom and configuring a system the next morning in the field at our local branches
* **Builder:** you have built integrations and reporting systems from scratch, and you know what it takes to go from zero to operational in a resource\-constrained environment
* **Owner:** when something breaks, you find out about it before anyone has to tell you. When a vendor slips or an integration breaks, you own it to resolution rather than relaying the vendor’s excuse, and you surface problems to leadership early rather than after they compound
* **Communicator:** you explain complex technology decisions in plain language, and you approach non\-technical colleagues with patience and clarity — whether they run a branch or sit on the leadership team
* **Resourceful:** you do not default to needing more headcount when there is a gap — you find a way with what you have, then build the system that prevents the gap from coming back
* **Coachable:** you will work with a technical operating partner and an executive team who will challenge you, and you get curious rather than defensive when someone tells you that you are wrong
* **Dependable and team\-first:** crews get paid on time because the systems work. You show up the same way for the high\-visibility work and the unglamorous implementation detail, you share what you know freely, and you never let the systems live only in your head

Stord is The Consumer Experience Company, powering seamless checkout through delivery for today's leading brands. Stord is rapidly growing and is on track to double our revenue in the next 18 months. To meet and exceed this target, Stord is strategically scaling teams across the entire company, and seeking energetic experts to help us achieve our mission.


By combining comprehensive commerce\-enablement technology with high\-volume fulfillment services, Stord provides brands a platform to compete with retail giants. Stord manages over $10 billion of commerce annually through its fulfillment, warehousing, transportation, and operator\-built software suite including OMS, Pre\- and Post\-Purchase, and WMS platforms. Stord is leveling the playing field for all brands to deliver the best consumer experience at scale.


With Stord, brands can increase cart conversion, improve unit economics, and drive sustained customer loyalty. Stord’s end\-to\-end commerce solutions combine best\-in\-class omnichannel fulfillment and shipping with leading technology to ensure fast shipping, reliable delivery promises, easy access to more channels, and improved margins on every order.


Hundreds of leading DTC and B2B companies like AG1, True Classic, Native, Seed Health, quip, goodr, Sundays for Dogs, and more trust Stord to deliver industry\-leading consumer experiences on every order. Stord is headquartered in Atlanta with facilities across the United States, Canada, and Europe. Stord is backed by top\-tier investors including Kleiner Perkins, Franklin Templeton, Founders Fund, Strike Capital, Baillie Gifford, and Salesforce Ventures.


Role Overview
  

The Program Manager, Compliance is a strategic driver of Stord’s operational strength and commercial growth. This role is responsible for scaling enterprise compliance programs across OSHA, EPA, GMP, and adjacent regulatory regimes \- building the infrastructure that enables Stord to operate with confidence, win in the market, and deliver on the compliance commitments that today’s leading brands require from a fulfillment partner. A mature, well\-run compliance program is not just a risk management function at Stord; it is a competitive differentiator that unlocks customer revenue, supports network expansion, and protects the business at scale.
  

  

Reporting to the Director of Health, Safety \& Security, this is an enterprise\-level, network\-wide role that operates at the intersection of compliance, operations, and growth. The Program Manager partners closely with Sales, Customer Success, Operations, and Finance to ensure compliance capabilities are a strength Stord leads with \- enabling the business to pursue regulated customer segments, scale into new markets, and demonstrate the program maturity that top\-tier brands demand. The work product of this role is what the entire organization is built around: scalable written programs, audit frameworks, certification standards, reporting infrastructure, and regulatory intelligence systems that grow stronger as Stord grows.
**What This Role Owns**
=======================

This role owns the enterprise compliance program architecture \- the standards, written programs, audit frameworks, and governance mechanisms that define what ‘compliant’ looks like at every Stord facility. The work product of this role is what the rest of the organization is held accountable to. Specifically:


* Enterprise compliance program design, construction, and ownership across OSHA, EPA, GMP, GDP, DOT, and applicable state and local regulatory frameworks \- building programs from the ground up where gaps exist and elevating inconsistent standards to enterprise\-grade.
* Regulatory intelligence: continuously monitoring rulemaking, agency guidance, and enforcement trends; converting regulatory change into updated enterprise programs before gaps become violations.
* Enterprise audit and inspection framework: designing the internal audit program architecture, defining scope and methodology, and building the tools and cadences that keep the network inspection\-ready \- not conducting site audits, but building the system that governs them.
* Enterprise compliance documentation infrastructure: designing and owning the system of record for all written programs, SOPs, training requirements, certifications, and regulatory correspondence \- the single source of truth for compliance across the network.
* Customer and industry certification programs: GMP, GDP, CTPAT, TAPA, and other regulated operating standards required by Stord’s customer base.
* Regulatory agency relationships: serving as the primary compliance point of contact for OSHA, EPA, and other agencies at the program level.
* Enterprise compliance reporting, data, and dashboards: building the metrics infrastructure that gives the Head of HSS, senior leadership, and the broader business real\-time visibility into compliance performance, risk posture, and program health across the network.
* Enterprise compliance training architecture: defining what training is required, for whom, at what frequency, and in what format \- building the content and governance framework that regional and site teams deliver against.

**Key Responsibilities**
========================

**OSHA Compliance Program Management**
--------------------------------------

* Build and own Stord’s enterprise OSHA compliance program \- designing the written program architecture, establishing network\-wide standards, and creating the governance mechanisms that ensure consistent compliance across every facility regardless of size, volume, or operational complexity.

new_jobs.description:
In a world of possibilities, pursue one with endless opportunities. Imagine Next!  



At Parsons, you can imagine a career where you thrive, work with exceptional people, and be yourself. Guided by our leadership vision of valuing people, embracing agility, and fostering growth, we cultivate an innovative culture that empowers you to achieve your full potential. Unleash your talent and redefine what’s possible.  



**Job Description:**


Parsons is seeking a highly qualified **Program Manager** to lead Construction Management Services (CMS) in support of a major U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) program. The Program Manager will be responsible for the overall management, coordination, and execution of CMS task orders under an Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ), Multiple Award Task Order Contract (MATOC), ensuring compliance with all contract requirements, Federal regulations, and USACE standards.

  

  

**What You’ll be Doing**


* **Program Leadership:** Provide overall management and leadership for all CMS activities, ensuring compliance with USACE, Federal, and contract\-specific requirements.
* **Staffing \& Coordination:** Oversee recruiting, staffing, and coordination of CMS personnel to meet all experience, performance, and responsibility requirements for each task order. Lead bi\-weekly meetings as requested by the Contracting Officer and track payment invoices for all task orders, providing monthly reports on contract totals and remaining capacity.
* **Quality Assurance:** Ensure the implementation of Quality Assurance (QA) procedures in accordance with the Government Project Specific Quality Assurance Plan (PSQAP), ER 1180\-1\-6, and other applicable regulations.
* **Contract Administration:** Support the Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR) in contract administration, including review of submittals, progress schedules, safety plans, and contract modifications.
* **Reporting \& Documentation:** Oversee the preparation and submission of required documentation and reports, including daily QA reports, pre\-construction plan reviews, and correspondence for COR signature, using MS Word/Excel, USACE RMS, and other approved formats.
* **Risk Management:** Identify program risks and develop mitigation strategies, including those related to schedule, cost, safety, and quality.
* **Stakeholder Engagement:** Serve as the primary point of contact for coordination with Government personnel, subcontractors, and other stakeholders.
* **Compliance:** Ensure all personnel meet required training (e.g., USACE Construction Quality Management for Contractors, safety, and ethics), security clearance, and background check requirements.
* **Veterans Employment:** Promote the training and employment of U.S. veterans in accordance with USACE guidance.
  

  

What Required Skills You'll Bring:


* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Construction Management, or related field.
* Must have a current/active Secret Clearance or above
* Must be able to travel up to 50% of the time.
* 15\+ years with a minimum of 5 years of experience in program management for construction management services, with at least 10 years preferred for senior\-level consideration. Experience must include oversight of large, complex construction programs, preferably for Federal or military clients
* Demonstrated ability to manage multi\-disciplinary teams and multiple concurrent task orders.
* Strong knowledge of Federal Acquisition Regulations (FAR), USACE practices, and applicable codes/standards.
* Excellent written and oral communication skills.
* Proficiency in project management tools and USACE RMS.
* Ability to obtain and maintain additional security clearances as required by specific task orders.
* Commitment to maintaining a safety\-minded management team and culture.
* Completion of USACE Construction Quality Management for Contractors course (within last 5 years)
* Minimum 10 hours of recent safety training (within last 2 years)
  

  

What Desired Skills You'll Bring:


* Active TS/SCI clearance
* Professional Registration as PE or RA
* Certification as PMP and/or CCM
* Experience managing large programs using Progressive Design Build, CM at Risk, or other early contractor involvement

**Security Clearance Requirement:**


An active Secret security clearance is required for this position.
